question: What is the primary purpose of nursing documentation in a healthcare setting?

options.B: Providing a legal record of patient care

explanation: Documentation acts as an official legal account of all interventions and observations concerning the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why does poor nursing documentation threaten patient safety during shift changes?

options.A: It breaks the continuity of planned clinical care
options.B: It prevents doctors from writing new prescriptions
options.C: It automatically delays the administration of oral drugs
options.D: It causes immediate financial loss to the hospital

explanation: Incomplete records leave incoming staff unaware of critical changes in the patient condition, risking missed care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: A patient record serves as legal evidence primarily because it shows what fact?

options.A: The exact nursing care administered to the patient
options.B: The personal opinions of the attending physician
options.C: The financial status of the patient relatives
options.D: The political affiliations of the ward staff

explanation: Courts rely on medical records to verify the timing and nature of interventions performed by healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: How do hospital managers use completed patient health records for quality improvement?

options.A: Deciding which wards receive new television sets
options.B: Conducting clinical audits to check care standards
options.C: Punishing nurses who make minor spelling mistakes
options.D: Calculating the daily menu requirements for patients

explanation: Auditing records reveals patterns in clinical outcomes, helping administrators enhance hospital protocols and patient safety. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the legal implication of an omitted nursing intervention in a patient chart?

options.A: Legally, the care is considered never performed
options.B: The doctor takes full responsibility for the omission
options.C: The nurse can simply explain it verbally in court
options.D: The hospital automatically assumes another ward did it

explanation: In legal proceedings, unrecorded care is treated as nonexistent, exposing the nurse to negligence claims. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: A nurse realizes an entry was missed three hours ago. What is the correct action?

options.A: Write a late entry noting the exact current and past time
options.B: Squeeze the notes into the tiny margins of earlier pages
options.C: Ask a colleague to sign the missed entry for today
options.D: Backdate the signature to match the time of the event

explanation: Late entries must be clearly marked as such, indicating both the current time and the time the event actually occurred. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which entry represents factual and objective nursing documentation?

options.A: Patient is very lazy and refuses to walk around
options.B: Wound on left heel measures 3cm by 2cm with foul odor
options.C: Patient looks much better today than yesterday morning
options.D: The relatives are annoying and disturbing the ward

explanation: Objective documentation focuses on observable, measurable facts rather than personal judgments or emotional opinions. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is it discouraged to document care hours before it is actually performed?

options.A: The doctor will refuse to sign the treatment chart
options.B: Hospital printers will reject the advance entries
options.C: Pens might run out of ink before the shift ends
options.D: Plans can change suddenly and lead to falsified records

explanation: Documenting before execution creates a false record if the patient condition changes or the procedure gets cancelled. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: What does the letter 'O' stand for in the SOAP charting format?
explanation: In SOAP charting, O stands for objective data, which includes measurable and observable findings like vital signs. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: How does charting by exception differ from traditional narrative nursing notes?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for patient vital sign charts
options.B: It prevents doctors from reading notes written by students
options.C: It only requires documentation of abnormal or deviant findings
options.D: It forces nurses to write long stories about every routine bath

explanation: Charting by exception uses preprinted standards, saving time by recording only variances from expected norms. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' represent at the beginning of the ISBAR handover tool?
explanation: ISBAR begins with Situation, allowing the nurse to state clearly what is happening right now with the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why should shift handovers take place in a private office rather than the open ward?

options.A: To allow nurses to eat breakfast while listening to updates
options.B: To ensure doctors can interrupt the nursing report easily
options.C: To prevent junior student nurses from hearing medical terms
options.D: To protect patient confidentiality and prevent privacy breaches

explanation: Discussing clinical details in public areas violates medical confidentiality ethics by exposing private health data to visitors. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: Where should an incident report regarding a medication error be filed?

options.A: On the front cover of the daily ward attendance book
options.B: Inside the personal file of the head nursing officer
options.C: Inside the clinical nursing notes of the patient chart
options.D: In the hospital administrative risk management records

explanation: Incident reports remain strictly administrative and are kept separate from the patient medical record. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why is it incorrect to write in the patient chart that an incident report was filed?

options.A: It stops the doctor from prescribing correct antidote drugs
options.B: It prevents the patient from getting discharged on time
options.C: It immediately invalidates the vital sign summary sheets
options.D: It creates an unnecessary legal trail pointing to internal audits

explanation: Charting the existence of an incident report in the patient file can complicate legal discovery processes during investigations. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the correct procedure for correcting a written mistake in a paper nursing record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the whole shift
options.B: Apply liquid correction fluid over the wrong word
options.C: Draw a single line through the error and sign it
options.D: Scrape the paper with a razor blade until it is clean

explanation: A single line allows the original entry to remain visible while clearly indicating it has been invalidated. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why are blank spaces left in handwritten nursing notes considered dangerous?

options.A: Ink will bleed through the paper and stain the table
options.B: It makes the page look untidy during doctor rounds
options.C: Someone else can easily add unauthorized text later
options.D: The hospital auditor will fine the ward for neatness

explanation: Leaving empty lines invites tampering, as malicious persons could insert false information into the record. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)
